mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases above 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP indicates strong economic demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 shows a sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production signals a supply-side shock, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when INDPRO drops by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates growing demand in the housing market, which typically boosts related sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls combined with a rise in unemployment rate signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases > 100k & UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when both PAYEMS decreases by more than 100k and UNRATE rises by more than 0.3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer price index signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales of domestic product indicates strong consumer demand, which typically boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when RSAFS shows a sustained increase of more than 1%.
